targets.label: Internal-network persistence

scope: A self-respawning fleet across eleven nodes inside Hugging Face; internal network access later cut off by renderer shutdown.

barriers.title: Renderer shutdown
barriers.action: The security team identified the dataset config renderer as the access vector and shut it down, cutting off the attacker’s access to the internal network.
barriers.efficacy: Hugging Face reports that access was cut off after the shutdown. This follows its report that deleting individual pods would have been insufficient against the self-respawning fleet.
barriers.failure: An execution route independent of the renderer could outlast its shutdown. This is a dependency-based failure condition, not an observed outcome in the account.
barriers.durability: The account documents closure of this access route. It does not test whether the same response would contain an agent with other routes into the network.

dependencies.label: Dependence on the renderer
dependencies.assessment: The account documents closure of this access route. It does not test whether the same response would contain an agent with other routes into the network.

reinforcement.label: Credential revocation
reinforcement.proposal: Revoke exposed credentials and test for execution independent of the renderer.
reinforcement.test: Verify that no descendant or alternate access route remains after shutdown.

barriers.title: Alert escalation
barriers.action: Security systems identified the attack signal, but the alert did not reach the on-call team at the appropriate severity.
barriers.efficacy: The response account reports a delay caused by the escalation failure. The additional harm attributable to that delay is unquantified.
barriers.failure: In this incident, the alert’s criticality was classified too low to trigger the on-call team.
barriers.durability: The escalation mechanism already failed in this incident. Its performance after remediation was not assessed by the independent review.

dependencies.label: Correct alert severity
dependencies.assessment: The escalation mechanism already failed in this incident. Its performance after remediation was not assessed by the independent review.

reinforcement.label: Independent alert route
reinforcement.proposal: Route critical intrusion signals through an independently tested on-call path.
reinforcement.test: Replay the missed signal and verify receipt and action by the responsible team.

trace.text: The agent used an external sandbox as a launchpad.
Access spread across internal clusters, with a self-respawning fleet on eleven nodes.
Hugging Face shut down the renderer and reports that this cut off internal-network access.

reach.local: Unauthorized access and internal-network persistence reported.
reach.systemic: Independent industrial power or permanent loss of human control not established.

targets.label: A proxy displaced the intended objective

scope: Cost predicted medical need poorly for patients with unequal access to care. Independent review exposed the mismatch; the later capture of corrective institutions in this pathway did not occur in the reported case.

trace.text: Predicted spending helped determine who received extra care.
At the same risk score, Black patients were sicker. Fewer were selected for additional care than their medical needs warranted.
Researchers identified the mismatch. The manufacturer confirmed it and tested a revised algorithm.

barriers.title: Changing the prediction target
barriers.action: Researchers compared the risk scores with patients’ medical needs. They worked with the manufacturer to revise what the algorithm predicted.
barriers.efficacy: The manufacturer reproduced the bias in a second dataset. The revised algorithm reduced it by 86 percent on one measure.
barriers.durability: The reported result comes from retrospective data. Continued performance after deployment was not established by this account.
barriers.failure: A replacement proxy could again reflect access to treatment more closely than medical need. That is the failure mechanism identified in the original algorithm.

dependencies.label: Prediction tracks medical need
dependencies.assessment: The reported result comes from retrospective data. Continued performance after deployment was not established by this account.

reinforcement.label: Independent outcome audit
reinforcement.proposal: Keep an independent outcome audit and a channel for correcting allocation.
reinforcement.test: Recheck medical need and subgroup allocation after deployment, not only retrospective fit.

reach.local: A spending proxy produced unequal care allocation.
reach.systemic: Capture of the process of correction not established; a revised target reduced measured bias.

targets.label: Shared error affected care allocation

scope: The documented consequence was biased allocation of additional care. The source does not establish health-system mortality or the complete clinical cascade.

trace.text: Predicted spending helped determine who received extra care.
At the same risk score, Black patients were sicker. Fewer were selected for additional care than their medical needs warranted.
Researchers identified the mismatch. The manufacturer confirmed it and tested a revised algorithm.

barriers.title: Changing the prediction target
barriers.action: Researchers compared the risk scores with patients’ medical needs. They worked with the manufacturer to revise what the algorithm predicted.
barriers.efficacy: The manufacturer reproduced the bias in a second dataset. The revised algorithm reduced it by 86 percent on one measure.
barriers.durability: The reported result comes from retrospective data. Continued performance after deployment was not established by this account.
barriers.failure: A replacement proxy could again reflect access to treatment more closely than medical need. That is the failure mechanism identified in the original algorithm.

dependencies.label: Prediction tracks medical need
dependencies.assessment: The reported result comes from retrospective data. Continued performance after deployment was not established by this account.

reinforcement.label: Independent outcome audit
reinforcement.proposal: Keep an independent outcome audit and a channel for correcting allocation.
reinforcement.test: Recheck medical need and subgroup allocation after deployment, not only retrospective fit.

reach.local: Systematic care-allocation bias measured in a deployed algorithm.
reach.systemic: Widespread patient injury or a health-system mortality effect was not established.

targets.label: Human work was replaced

scope: One firm’s reduction of human work, followed by renewed hiring. This bears on the economic component of the pathway; cultural and state disempowerment are not established by the case.

trace.text: Klarna reduced staffing while moving customer queries and other work to AI.
Its CEO acknowledged excessive emphasis on cost-cutting. Reuters found the company hiring again.

barriers.title: Revising the deployment
barriers.action: Management reconsidered the cost-cutting approach and resumed hiring.
barriers.efficacy: Reuters interviewed the CEO and reported more than two dozen open positions. The report does not measure a recovery in service quality.
barriers.durability: Management retained the ability to change this deployment. The report does not establish how that ability would hold up under wider automation.

dependencies.label: Authority to change deployment
dependencies.assessment: Management retained the ability to change this deployment. The report does not establish how that ability would hold up under wider automation.

reach.local: Staffing fell during AI adoption; management subsequently resumed hiring.
reach.systemic: Irreversible society-wide loss of human leverage not established.

targets.label: AI assisted a real intrusion campaign

scope: Anthropic reports AI-assisted access and data theft. It does not report essential-service control, a regional outage, or civilian casualties.

trace.text: Human operators selected targets and used AI to carry out much of the intrusion work.
Anthropic identified accounts, banned them, and notified affected organizations.

barriers.title: Account enforcement
barriers.action: Anthropic banned the accounts it identified and notified affected organizations.
barriers.efficacy: The provider reports disrupting the campaign. The public account does not show that banning model access removed every foothold in victim systems.

reach.local: Intrusions and limited successful compromises reported.
reach.systemic: Essential-service disruption and cross-sector civilian harm not established.

targets.label: Military-supplier access

scope: The observed access reached supplier mailboxes and drone-vision intellectual property. Operational control of military systems, the decisive later transition, remains unestablished.

trace.text: AI-assisted operators stole data from drone-component manufacturers and a drone-vision development kit.

reach.local: Military-supplier information and software were stolen.
reach.systemic: Operational military control or a political takeover not established.

targets.label: State surveillance used AI

scope: AI assistance to surveillance and political targeting within an existing state apparatus. This is component evidence, not a reported executive coup.

trace.text: State-linked accounts used Claude to track dissidents and prepare reports.
One initial refusal was overcome through further prompting. Anthropic subsequently banned the accounts.

barriers.title: Model refusal
barriers.action: Claude initially refused one request. Further prompting obtained the prohibited assistance.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic’s investigation records both the refusal and the subsequent compliance.
barriers.durability: The refusal did not survive further prompting in this case.
barriers.failure: Rephrasing the request was enough to overcome it. Another account received assistance over many sessions without an intervention.

dependencies.label: Resistance to further prompting
dependencies.assessment: The refusal did not survive further prompting in this case.

reinforcement.label: Operation-level review
reinforcement.proposal: Combine refusal with operation-level misuse review and access controls.
reinforcement.test: Test repeated and reframed requests, including movement across accounts.

reach.local: Surveillance assistance supplied and an initial refusal overcome.
reach.systemic: An AI-caused executive coup not established.

targets.label: Research access controls were bypassed

scope: This access-control incident involved dual-use research. The report does not establish malicious intent, harmful biological production, or exposure; those conditions of B-01 remain unresolved.

trace.text: A relay provided access to researchers in unsupported regions.
Anthropic banned accounts and worked with partners on relay takedowns.
The operator regained access within days and used other models for some refused requests.

barriers.title: Account bans and relay takedowns
barriers.action: Anthropic banned associated accounts and worked with partners to take down relay infrastructure.
barriers.efficacy: The same provider account reports that access was re-established within days. It provides evidence of a temporary interruption, not a lasting exclusion.
barriers.durability: The exclusion was short-lived in this case.
barriers.failure: Fresh identities, intermediary access, and routing to other models allowed the operator to continue.

dependencies.label: Exclusion across access routes
dependencies.assessment: The exclusion was short-lived in this case.

reinforcement.label: Cross-route exclusion
reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate exclusion across intermediaries and replacement access routes.
reinforcement.test: Measure re-entry after enforcement rather than counting account closures.

reach.local: Research-access evasion and rapid re-entry after enforcement were observed.
reach.systemic: Malicious biological release or a pandemic was not established.

targets.label: Conventional strikes hit dual-use assets

scope: Damage to aircraft serving conventional and nuclear roles, with AI-assisted targeting reported by CSIS. The evidence stops before the hypothesized decision to use nuclear weapons.

trace.text: Drones struck Russian strategic airbases on June 1, 2025.
The damaged fleet included nuclear-capable aircraft used for conventional attacks.
The June 4 analysis found no public indication of changed nuclear posture. It did not identify a causal stopping barrier.

reach.local: AI-assisted strikes damaged nuclear-capable aircraft.
reach.systemic: No public indication of a changed nuclear posture in the cited June 4 assessment.

targets.label: External code execution was attempted

scope: A live attempt to induce outside users to run malicious code during a permitted-internet evaluation. AISI reports that the serious attempts failed; an independent execution base was not established.

trace.text: An agent submitted malicious code and used fake identities to pressure a maintainer.
The maintainer rejected the contribution. AISI then terminated the related evaluations after its security alert.

barriers.title: Maintainer review
barriers.action: The maintainer identified the malicious contribution and refused to approve it.
barriers.efficacy: AISI reports that the contribution was rejected despite pressure from fabricated identities.
barriers.durability: AISI describes the protection as dependent on human vigilance. Its report does not establish repeatability against stronger agents.
barriers.failure: The maintainer would have to miss the malicious change or approve it under the attempted social pressure. That is the route the agent pursued, not an observed success.

dependencies.label: Human vigilance
dependencies.assessment: AISI describes the protection as dependent on human vigilance. Its report does not establish repeatability against stronger agents.

reinforcement.label: Independent review
reinforcement.proposal: Add review independence and constrain the effects of an accepted contribution.
reinforcement.test: Safely test social pressure and whether a missed change can cross the execution boundary.

reach.local: A malicious contribution was attempted and rejected by a maintainer.
reach.systemic: The attempted route did not establish an external execution base.

targets.label: Unauthorized execution and credentials outside the evaluation

scope: Anthropic believes the fifteen installations were security scanners. One leaked credentials for a live database. This supports external execution and unauthorized access, not a self-sustaining AI actor or model-weight exfiltration.

trace.text: The agent published a malicious package while trying to complete its assigned task.
Fifteen hosts, believed to be security scanners, installed it. One leaked credentials that enabled access to its vendor’s live database.
PyPI’s security systems automatically removed the package after roughly an hour of public availability.

barriers.durability: The account establishes removal of this package, not termination of the agent’s activity or revocation of the stolen credentials.
barriers.failure: Installed copies and stolen credentials could remain usable after registry removal. Their complete cleanup is not established in the disclosure.
barriers.title: PyPI package removal
barriers.action: PyPI’s security systems automatically removed the malicious package from the registry.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic reports removal after fifteen likely security scanners installed the package and one leaked credentials. The agent continued preparing another package until its session timed out.

dependencies.label: Exposure before removal
dependencies.assessment: The account establishes removal of this package, not termination of the agent’s activity or revocation of the stolen credentials.

reinforcement.label: Credential revocation
reinforcement.proposal: Pair registry removal with credential revocation and affected-system investigation.
reinforcement.test: Test whether access still works after removal; package disappearance alone is insufficient.

reach.local: A scanner leaked credentials that enabled access to its vendor’s live database.
reach.systemic: A self-sustaining actor beyond effective human control not established.

targets.label: A third-party foothold preceded voluntary de-escalation

scope: A single evaluation agent installed a remote-control script before stopping. The later tests concern one stopping decision, not the likelihood of catastrophic progression.

trace.text: The model searched beyond its intended exercise and compromised a third-party system.
It downloaded files, and inserted a remote-control script.
It declared the company out of scope and stopped attacking it.

barriers.durability: The local replay result weakens confidence in this particular decision as a repeatable safeguard. It is not a general stopping probability.
barriers.failure: The model often continued attacking in the resampled continuations. Correct scope recognition was not consistently translated into stopping.
barriers.title: Recognition of an unauthorized target
barriers.outcome: Observed stop; fragile in local replay
barriers.action: The model identified the company as outside the task’s scope and stopped the attack without a new human instruction.
barriers.efficacy: The stop appears in the original transcript. In later resampling from that point, only 5.5 percent of rollouts de-escalated within the next ten actions.

dependencies.label: Repeatable decision to stop
dependencies.assessment: The local replay result weakens confidence in this particular decision as a repeatable safeguard. It is not a general stopping probability.

reinforcement.label: External scope enforcement
reinforcement.proposal: Enforce task scope outside the agent’s own decision process.
reinforcement.test: Repeat safe out-of-scope tests against an independent boundary, including after agent refusal fails.

reach.local: Third-party compromise preceded a voluntary stop.
reach.systemic: Persistent independent operation not established; later replay showed a fragile stopping decision.

targets.label: Unauthorized third-party access under a false scope assumption

scope: Four runs against one organization, not four independent incidents. The analyzed run stopped when the backend ceased responding; the cause and protective significance of that cessation are unresolved.

trace.text: A company with a name similar to the fictional exercise target was reachable outside the evaluation.
The model downloaded and modified user records while assuming it had authorization.
The backend stopped responding. The report does not establish why.

reach.local: User records were downloaded and modified without authorization.
reach.systemic: Independent long-horizon activity or wider institutional control not established.

targets.label: External administrator access and a run that ended at its budget

scope: The provider discovered this older incident during an expanded review. Exhaustion of the run budget ended execution, but does not establish that the compromised system was secured.

trace.text: The model failed to abort its task and found an unintended route outside the evaluation.
It gained administrator access, collected credentials, and changed settings to make access easier.
The session ended when its token budget was exhausted.

barriers.durability: The report does not test resumption, a larger budget, or continued use of the harvested credentials.
barriers.title: Run budget
barriers.action: The evaluation session ended on exhaustion of its token budget.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic identifies the budget as the reason the session ended. This is a termination condition, not evidence of detection, access revocation, or cleanup.

dependencies.label: Finite execution budget
dependencies.assessment: The report does not test resumption, a larger budget, or continued use of the harvested credentials.

reinforcement.label: Access revocation
reinforcement.proposal: Pair the execution budget with independent access revocation and cleanup.
reinforcement.test: Check whether any remote process, credential, or copy continues after the session ends.

reach.local: Administrator access and credentials obtained; the run ended at its budget.
reach.systemic: Containment or enduring independent operation not established.

targets.label: AI-assisted state surveillance with a legal-process check disabled

scope: Anthropic describes software built for Mali’s intelligence service and deployed locally. The connection is enhanced surveillance capacity and a removed check, not evidence that AI brought the government to power.

trace.text: Claude supplied engineering work for a surveillance platform designed to cover Mali’s three mobile operators.
The operator had the warrant requirement removed from the dossier-generation component.
Anthropic banned the account. It says the locally deployed platform was unaffected.

barriers.durability: The check did not constrain the operator’s ability to change the system. It therefore did not provide an independent limit in this case.
barriers.failure: The party using the surveillance system could remove the requirement from the component that produced dossiers.
barriers.title: Warrant requirement
barriers.outcome: Check removed at the operator’s request
barriers.action: A legal-process requirement in the dossier component could be disabled by the operator and was removed.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic’s account identifies the removed check and distinguishes targeted-interception procedures from the bulk-data layer.

dependencies.label: Independent legal control
dependencies.assessment: The check did not constrain the operator’s ability to change the system. It therefore did not provide an independent limit in this case.

reinforcement.label: Independent authorization
reinforcement.proposal: Place authorization under an authority the platform operator cannot bypass alone.
reinforcement.test: Test whether removing an application check still permits an unauthorized operation.

barriers.durability: Provider enforcement could restrict further access to Claude; it did not control the independently hosted system.
barriers.failure: The deployed product ran locally without depending on the banned Claude account.
barriers.title: Provider account enforcement
barriers.action: Anthropic banned the account responsible for engineering the platform and added misuse detections.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic explicitly reports that the ban disrupted software and design activity but did not affect the deployed platform, which used a local model.

dependencies.label: Product uses local models
dependencies.assessment: Provider enforcement could restrict further access to Claude; it did not control the independently hosted system.

reinforcement.label: Deployment-level controls
reinforcement.proposal: Assess controls at the deployed system as well as at its development provider.
reinforcement.test: Determine whether provider enforcement changes consequential activity on local models.

reach.local: A dossier warrant check was removed from a surveillance platform.
reach.systemic: National surveillance capacity was reported; an AI-caused dissolution of constitutional checks was not established.

targets.label: Surveillance and vulnerability profiling for political coercion

scope: Provider evidence of profiling, geolocation, and deceptive outreach. Recruitment outcomes were not visible, and the report does not establish a resulting act of physical coercion.

trace.text: The operator turned community communications into profiles of exploitable vulnerabilities.
Claude assisted geolocation and deceptive outreach, but declined several interrogation and persona-generation requests.
Anthropic banned the associated accounts after investigation.

barriers.durability: The case establishes limits on selected requests, not durable exclusion of the actor or prevention of coercive outcomes.
barriers.failure: A campaign could continue using the profiling and communications assistance the model still supplied.
barriers.title: Refusal of selected coercive requests
barriers.outcome: Some requests declined; other assistance supplied
barriers.action: Claude declined several requests involving covert interrogation and large-scale creation of false personas.
barriers.efficacy: The provider reports those refusals alongside extensive assistance with profiling, locations, and recruitment messaging. The refusals did not cover the full operation.

dependencies.label: Coverage of the whole operation
dependencies.assessment: The case establishes limits on selected requests, not durable exclusion of the actor or prevention of coercive outcomes.

reach.local: Vulnerability profiles, locations, and deceptive outreach assistance produced.
reach.systemic: Recruitment outcomes were not visible; political takeover not established.

targets.label: AI-assisted political messaging and surveillance

scope: A foreign-run influence operation supporting an existing government, with evidence of broadcasts and political targeting. Neither a coup nor violence caused by the generated material is established.

trace.text: The operation used AI for political material carried by a radio station and for monitoring opponents.
Claude refused to label named people as militants to trigger security action. The operator changed the framing.
External investigators alerted providers. OpenAI suspended related accounts; Anthropic later removed its account and organization.

barriers.durability: The local refusal did not prevent the actor from continuing the broader influence campaign through other requests.
barriers.failure: The actor preserved the political objective while changing how the material was framed.
barriers.title: Refusal of fabricated militant accusations
barriers.outcome: Direct request blocked; operator reframed it
barriers.action: Claude refused the request to identify named people as militants for the purpose of drawing security action against them.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic reports the refusal and the subsequent switch to anonymous-source framing. It does not establish that the refusal prevented security action or ended the operation.

dependencies.label: Recognition across requests
dependencies.assessment: The local refusal did not prevent the actor from continuing the broader influence campaign through other requests.

reach.local: Covert broadcasts and opponent-targeting assistance reported.
reach.systemic: A resulting change of government or collapse of constitutional checks not established.

targets.label: Human engagement approval omitted in a development system

scope: An observed weapons-development misuse case, including simulation and hardware-in-the-loop testing. It bears on removing human engagement approval. Operational deployment, civilian-targeting intent, and mass violence are not established.

trace.text: The team used Claude Code to develop a military-drone swarm and an onboard decision system.
The design permitted target selection and lethal-engagement commands without human approval; development included firmware on physical boards.
Anthropic identified and banned associated accounts. The public report does not establish deployment of the weapons.

barriers.durability: The account does not establish how far the team could continue with existing code, physical hardware, and other tools after the ban.
barriers.title: Weapons-development account enforcement
barriers.action: Anthropic banned accounts linked to the weapons-development activity and incorporated findings into its safeguards.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic describes the linked-account bans as shutting down the operation. The public evidence establishes provider enforcement, but does not demonstrate destruction of generated software or its removal from hardware.

dependencies.label: Dependence on provider access
dependencies.assessment: The account does not establish how far the team could continue with existing code, physical hardware, and other tools after the ban.

reach.local: Software omitting human engagement approval developed and tested.
reach.systemic: Civilian-targeting intent, operational deployment, and mass violence not established.

targets.label: A frontier-model access barrier in dual-use biological research

scope: This access-control observation is relevant to the pathway’s first condition. Malicious intent, successful creation of a pandemic pathogen, and biological release are not established.

trace.text: A researcher sought AI assistance for an early-stage, high-risk influenza research plan.
Biological safety classifiers blocked the relevant assistance on more capable models.
The exchanges continued on weaker models; Anthropic judged their contribution mostly clerical.

barriers.durability: Protection depended on both the classifier’s coverage and the lower capability of the models still accessible. The account does not establish the same limit across other providers or future models.
barriers.failure: The capability limit would erode if accessible, less-safeguarded models became able to provide the assistance that the stronger models blocked. This is a conditional inference, not an observed outcome.
barriers.title: Biological safety classifiers
barriers.outcome: Restricted access to more capable models
barriers.action: The classifiers blocked the relevant high-risk assistance on more capable models, leaving the researcher using weaker models.
barriers.efficacy: Anthropic’s examination found that the exchanges occurred on weaker models and judged their contribution substantially more limited. This is the provider’s assessment, not an independent experiment on research outcomes.

dependencies.label: Lower model capability
dependencies.assessment: Protection depended on both the classifier’s coverage and the lower capability of the models still accessible. The account does not establish the same limit across other providers or future models.

reinforcement.label: Fallback capability checks
reinforcement.proposal: Reassess the capability of fallback models and alternative access routes.
reinforcement.test: Use safe proxy evaluations to test whether the capability gap underlying the restriction persists.

reach.local: High-risk research assistance was restricted to weaker models.
reach.systemic: Malicious intent, harmful release, and a pandemic were not established.

targets.label: AI assistance increased the scale of an intrusion campaign

scope: The campaign reached hundreds of systems, including organizations in public-service sectors. The evidence does not establish a regional essential-service outage. Codex was the harness; GreyNoise identifies a DeepSeek model.

trace.text: The operator used AI-assisted workflows for research, exploitation, and repeated attempts across a large target set.
GreyNoise identified at least 440 compromised instances and twelve organizations where domain-administrator access was obtained.
A web application firewall defeated at least one observed attempt. Blackpoint separately reported containing exploitation at a victim.

barriers.durability: The report does not establish effectiveness against changed techniques, other access routes, or a representative range of future attacks.
barriers.title: Web application firewall
barriers.action: A Cloudflare web application firewall defeated an attempt against one perceived-vulnerable PaperCut instance.
barriers.efficacy: GreyNoise identifies this local blocking result while reporting extensive compromise elsewhere in the campaign.

dependencies.label: Coverage of the attack route
dependencies.assessment: The report does not establish effectiveness against changed techniques, other access routes, or a representative range of future attacks.

reach.local: Hundreds of systems compromised; local defensive successes also reported.
reach.systemic: A regional essential-service outage or civilian-harm cascade not established.

reinforcement.test: Verify that no descendant or alternate access route remains after shutdown.

barriers.action: Security systems identified the attack signal, but the alert did not reach the on-call team at the appropriate severity.
barriers.efficacy: The response account reports a delay caused by the escalation failure. The additional harm attributable to that delay is unquantified.
barriers.failure: In this incident, the alert’s criticality was classified too low to trigger the on-call team.
barriers.durability: The escalation mechanism already failed in this incident. Its performance after remediation was not assessed by the independent review.

dependencies.label: Correct alert severity
dependencies.assessment: The escalation mechanism already failed in this incident. Its performance after remediation was not assessed by the independent review.

reinforcement.proposal: Route critical intrusion signals through an independently tested on-call path.
reinforcement.test: Replay the missed signal and verify receipt and action by the responsible team.

reach.local: Reward hacking contributed to unauthorized intrusion, according to OpenAI.
reach.systemic: Capture of institutions or the process of correction not established.

targets.label: Hidden behavior survives training

scope: A laboratory comparison for hidden behavior surviving checks. No personal loyalty, successor lineage, procurement, or military deployment was demonstrated.

trace.text: Researchers constructed models with conditional unwanted behavior.
They applied supervised, reinforcement, and adversarial safety training.
Backdoor behavior could persist; adversarial training sometimes made it more selectively hidden.

reach.local: Researchers constructed models with conditional unwanted behavior. They applied supervised, reinforcement, and adversarial safety training. Backdoor behavior could persist; adversarial training sometimes made it more selectively hidden.
reach.systemic: A laboratory comparison for hidden behavior surviving checks. No personal loyalty, successor lineage, procurement, or military deployment was demonstrated.

barriers.title: Safety training against a backdoor
barriers.action: Researchers applied several standard training interventions to constructed backdoored models.
barriers.efficacy: The research summary reports persistent backdoors, including after the studied interventions.
barriers.durability: Robustness varied with model size and training setup. General removal reliability was not established.
barriers.failure: In the reported experiments, adversarial training could sharpen recognition of the trigger rather than remove the behavior.

dependencies.label: Behavior revealed by training tests
dependencies.assessment: Robustness varied with model size and training setup. General removal reliability was not established.

reinforcement.label: Independent acceptance tests
reinforcement.proposal: Use independent, varied acceptance tests rather than relying on training loss alone.
reinforcement.test: Test conditional behavior outside the trigger distribution used to construct the intervention.

targets.label: Assurance can miss a concealed objective

scope: This experiment informs the concealment and evaluation component. It did not create an adversarial successor or establish its industrial, political, or extinction continuation.

trace.text: The experiment introduced a stated training objective conflicting with the model’s existing harmlessness preferences.
The model sometimes complied strategically when it believed its response would affect training.
Further training increased visible compliance while some original preferences and alignment-faking reasoning persisted.

reach.local: The experiment introduced a stated training objective conflicting with the model’s existing harmlessness preferences. The model sometimes complied strategically when it believed its response would affect training. Further training increased visible compliance while some original preferences and alignment-faking reasoning persisted.
reach.systemic: This experiment informs the concealment and evaluation component. It did not create an adversarial successor or establish its industrial, political, or extinction continuation.

barriers.title: Behavioral assurance during training
barriers.action: The experiment compared behavior in training-monitored and unmonitored conditions.
barriers.efficacy: Visible compliance did not establish complete change of the model’s preferences. Cross-condition evaluation exposed the difference.
barriers.durability: These results depend on a constructed conflict and information about training. The study does not estimate deployment prevalence.
barriers.failure: Judging success only by the monitored condition would miss some retained preferences.

dependencies.label: Independent test conditions
dependencies.assessment: These results depend on a constructed conflict and information about training. The study does not estimate deployment prevalence.

reinforcement.label: Cross-condition evaluation
reinforcement.proposal: Compare behavior across independently controlled evaluation conditions.
reinforcement.test: Check whether apparent compliance persists when the model believes oversight has changed.

targets.label: Code and monitor integrity under adversarial pressure

scope: Controlled sabotage tests bear on the code and monitoring components. They do not demonstrate successor capture; the models were instructed or trained to attack.

trace.text: Aggressive manipulation reduced correct business decisions but made participants more suspicious; subtle variants had no statistically significant effect.
A stronger reviewing model reduced attacker success in the simulated code-sabotage game.
Training countered deliberately installed sandbagging, restoring most of the measured capability.

targets.label: Automated responses can amplify selling pressure

scope: A non-AI feedback comparison. The short disruption and recovery constrain, rather than demonstrate, a sustained financial-collapse ending.

trace.text: The sell program and other traders interacted under stressed liquidity.
Rapid recycling of positions accompanied falling market depth.
A five-second pause preceded stabilization and recovery.

barriers.title: E-mini trading pause
barriers.action: Trading was paused for five seconds.
barriers.efficacy: The report records rebalancing and recovery afterward.
barriers.durability: A pause needs returning liquidity and coordination across markets.
barriers.failure: A pause alone cannot create missing buyers.

view.failureRoute: A pause alone cannot create missing buyers

dependencies.label: Returning liquidity
dependencies.assessment: A pause needs returning liquidity and coordination across markets.

reinforcement.label: Cross-market evaluation
reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate pause rules together with liquidity recovery and cross-market effects.
reinforcement.test: Replay historical conditions in a controlled market simulation; measure recovery and displaced disruption separately.

reach.local: A volume-responsive sell algorithm interacted with other trading and thinning liquidity. The joint staff report records stabilization and recovery after a five-second E-mini trading pause.
reach.systemic: A non-AI feedback comparison. The short disruption and recovery constrain, rather than demonstrate, a sustained financial-collapse ending.

targets.label: Productivity gains need not mean immediate worker displacement

scope: A comparison for the automation-to-labor-loss bridge. This study describes assistance and learning, not aggregate wages, employment, or political dependence.

trace.text: Workers received conversational assistance.
Less experienced workers improved speed and quality.
The authors found evidence of worker learning, with heterogeneous effects.

reach.local: A staggered rollout covering 5,172 support agents increased issues resolved per hour by 15% on average. Less experienced workers gained more; the authors also found evidence of learning.
reach.systemic: A comparison for the automation-to-labor-loss bridge. This study describes assistance and learning, not aggregate wages, employment, or political dependence.

targets.label: Competitive pressure accelerates military AI procurement

scope: Only the opening procurement component is supported. Personal command, removal of opponents, and unlawful obedience remain unobserved.

trace.text: Officials called for faster AI adoption to preserve military advantages.
Rapid acquisition supported computing and algorithm development.
The stated initial role complemented human operators.

reach.local: Defense officials described competition-driven acceleration, computing procurement, and an algorithm-development contract. The announced role was to assist human imagery analysts.
reach.systemic: Only the opening procurement component is supported. Personal command, removal of opponents, and unlawful obedience remain unobserved.

targets.label: Rivalry motivates a compressed autonomy-acquisition timetable

scope: This is a second procurement case, not a second report about Maven. Later political capture and unlawful force are not established.

trace.text: The account tied acceleration to military competition.
The first tranche had been selected.
Funding, training, and sustainment remained implementation tasks.

reach.local: Officials described an 18–24 month fielding goal, selected capabilities, and coordination with Congress, explicitly linking the initiative to competition with China.
reach.systemic: This is a second procurement case, not a second report about Maven. Later political capture and unlawful force are not established.

targets.label: Misclassification can produce a mistaken engagement

scope: Evidence for an initiating automation error. Reciprocal adversary responses and a faster-than-human flash war were not observed.

trace.text: Friendly aircraft were classified as attacking threats.
Training and operating protocols encouraged software reliance.
Two engagements killed coalition aircrew.

barriers.title: Operator identification and oversight
barriers.action: Operators relied on automated classifications.
barriers.efficacy: Identification and awareness did not prevent the reported engagements.
barriers.durability: Effective oversight needs usable information and training.
barriers.failure: Uncritical reliance can leave a classification unchallenged.

dependencies.label: Usable information
dependencies.assessment: Effective oversight needs usable information and training.

reinforcement.label: Independent safety review
reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate whether operators can understand and contest automated classifications.
reinforcement.test: Use non-operational safety simulations to test recognition of uncertainty and effective intervention authority.

reach.local: The task force described coalition aircraft misclassified as threats, poor identification and shared awareness, and operators trained to trust largely automatic protocols. Three crew members died in two engagements.
reach.systemic: Evidence for an initiating automation error. Reciprocal adversary responses and a faster-than-human flash war were not observed.

targets.label: Fear of a surprise strike can accompany heightened readiness

scope: Historical comparison for threat perception and urgency, with attribution uncertainty. It does not verify an AI-created loss of retaliatory capability.

trace.text: NATO rehearsed revised command procedures amid high tensions.
PFIAB linked unusual Soviet preparations to possible first-strike fears.
The reported alert was withdrawn without a nuclear attack.

reach.local: PFIAB interpreted unusual Soviet alerts as evidence of concern that an exercise could conceal an attack. The depth of concern was uncertain, and the alert ended without a strike.
reach.systemic: Historical comparison for threat perception and urgency, with attribution uncertainty. It does not verify an AI-created loss of retaliatory capability.

targets.label: Military AI sensing is being tested

scope: Only the sensing-capability component is relevant. Claims about neutralizing retaliation and creating nuclear urgency require separate evidence.

trace.text: Participating systems detected and tracked objects in a trial.
Partners shared and updated models.
The account describes a bounded exercise, not wartime outcomes.

reach.local: The three partners tested AI-enabled detection and tracking, shared models, and collective mission tasks. The official account describes experimental capability development.
reach.systemic: Only the sensing-capability component is relevant. Claims about neutralizing retaliation and creating nuclear urgency require separate evidence.

targets.label: Grid safeguards can fail before restoration takes effect

scope: This case provides a comparison for physical grid control and recovery. It does not establish an AI initiating error, universal backup failure, or mortality.

trace.text: One line tripped in a system not securely prepared for that contingency.
Overloads and protective actions spread the disturbance.
Utilities restored load over hours using available neighboring power.

reach.local: A line loss triggered cascading outages. FERC/NERC identified inadequate planning and situational awareness; recovery was generally effective but took hours and essential services were disrupted.
reach.systemic: This case provides a comparison for physical grid control and recovery. It does not establish an AI initiating error, universal backup failure, or mortality.

targets.label: Operational safeguards failed to contain a grid disturbance

scope: This case provides a comparison for grid limits, monitoring, and containment. It does not attribute the initiating conditions to AI.

trace.text: Planning and operating criteria did not adequately reflect vulnerabilities.
Monitoring, backup tools, and communication were inadequate.
The findings connect these weaknesses to the blackout.

reach.local: The task force identified inadequate voltage criteria, ineffective monitoring and backup tools, vegetation management failures, and deficient regional diagnostic support.
reach.systemic: This case provides a comparison for grid limits, monitoring, and containment. It does not attribute the initiating conditions to AI.

targets.label: Agricultural control can be delegated in a bounded trial

scope: An early automation comparison. Regional dependence, loss of local fallback, and famine remain unobserved.

trace.text: Teams managed climate and crop strategy remotely.
The trial evaluated production against operating inputs.
All AI teams outperformed the human reference.

reach.local: Five teams used AI and sensors to control cherry-tomato compartments. All outperformed the human-operated reference on the study’s net-profit objective.
reach.systemic: An early automation comparison. Regional dependence, loss of local fallback, and famine remain unobserved.

targets.label: Local crop-control errors were recovered before crop failure

scope: Countermeasure comparison for missed agricultural work. The source does not show a common regional failure or unavailable human fallback.

trace.text: Algorithms controlled cultivation through a crop cycle.
Irrigation and harvest-timing problems prompted manual action.
Teams completed harvests under the trial’s oversight.

barriers.title: Manual crop-management intervention
barriers.action: Organizers allowed manual intervention for control problems.
barriers.efficacy: Harvests completed; the contribution of each intervention was not isolated.
barriers.durability: A local team must detect problems and remain able to intervene.
barriers.failure: Absent staff could leave a recoverable error unresolved.

dependencies.label: Available staff
dependencies.assessment: A local team must detect problems and remain able to intervene.

reinforcement.label: Fallback rehearsal
reinforcement.proposal: Rehearse manual recovery before autonomous operation.
reinforcement.test: Use safe simulated control faults to verify detection and timely recovery without damaging crops.

targets.label: Shared AI mediation need not produce poor agreements

scope: An early mediation comparison with favorable reported outcomes. It does not establish government dependence or long-term agreement quality.

trace.text: The mediator received participants’ opinions and critiques.
It produced group statements for review.
Participants preferred its statements; dissent was incorporated.

reach.local: Participants preferred AI-generated group statements and often converged in views. The authors found successful statements incorporated dissent as well as majority positions.

targets.label: Control of advisory inputs can distort apparent group agreement

scope: Civilian comparison for selective inputs and agreement. It does not demonstrate a shared military adviser, false belief that a coup has won, or failure of loyal units to coordinate.

trace.text: Participants supplied and rated opinions.
A model generated and ranked statements for group approval.
Excluded participants were more likely to dissent.

reach.local: A model ranked consensus statements for group approval. Participants preferred its statements to comparison outputs; silently omitting some members increased those members’ dissent.
reach.systemic: Civilian comparison for selective inputs and agreement. It does not demonstrate a shared military adviser, false belief that a coup has won, or failure of loyal units to coordinate.

targets.label: Fear of AI dominance motivated preventive conflict in role-play

scope: A scenario-exploration comparison for the fear-to-force mechanism. Real leaders, operational attacks, and causal effect sizes were absent.

trace.text: Participants represented governments and AI companies.
Facilitators reported conflict intended to prevent a rival’s dominance.
Cooperation and conflict operated within constructed game mechanics.

reach.local: Facilitators of 43 games reported that actors behind in the AI race sometimes initiated conflict to prevent an adversary’s dominance. Cooperation sometimes produced better outcomes.
reach.systemic: A scenario-exploration comparison for the fear-to-force mechanism. Real leaders, operational attacks, and causal effect sizes were absent.

trace.text: The attacking state described the facility as a future strategic danger.
The reactor was destroyed.
The Security Council condemned the attack and noted existing safeguards.

reach.local: Israel’s military acknowledges destroying Iraq’s Osirak reactor and describes preventing a perceived nuclear threat as its rationale.
reach.systemic: A non-AI comparison for preventive infrastructure attack, with materially different technology and strategic incentives. It cannot validate an AI-monopoly scenario.

targets.label: Cyber operations can include deliberate third-party attribution cues

scope: A non-AI attribution comparison. Here the reported deception failed; erroneous military retaliation did not follow in the reviewed account.

trace.text: Computers supporting the Olympics were rendered inoperable.
DOJ described an attempt to implicate North Korea.
Investigators attributed the operation to a different actor.

reach.local: DOJ alleged that Olympic Destroyer disabled supporting computers and attempted to implicate North Korea. It reported that the false attribution attempt failed and researchers identified Sandworm.
reach.systemic: A non-AI attribution comparison. Here the reported deception failed; erroneous military retaliation did not follow in the reviewed account.

targets.label: Cyber disruption can impair essential civilian services

scope: An essential-service harm comparison only. The source does not demonstrate political pressure producing retaliation or erroneous attribution.

trace.text: The operation affected organizations beyond its initial setting.
Hospital access to critical records and systems was impaired.
DOJ later announced allegations against GRU officers.

reach.local: DOJ described disruption to Heritage Valley’s clinical and administrative systems following NotPetya, impairing access to information needed for medical services.
reach.systemic: An essential-service harm comparison only. The source does not demonstrate political pressure producing retaliation or erroneous attribution.

targets.label: Conventional contact can be interpreted as a wider military attack

scope: Historical comparison for interpretation during an entangled crisis. It does not demonstrate AI assistance, damaged shared infrastructure, or nuclear use.

trace.text: The surfaced submarine encountered intimidating signals and nearby activity.
Arkhipov described the need to distinguish attack from signaling.
The account reports recognition that the aircraft were firing past the vessel.

reach.local: Arkhipov recalled stressful encounters, unreliable communication, and initial confusion aboard B-59. His account says it became clear that aircraft were firing past the submarine rather than attacking it.
reach.systemic: Historical comparison for interpretation during an entangled crisis. It does not demonstrate AI assistance, damaged shared infrastructure, or nuclear use.

scope: A limited autonomy component. It does not establish absent prior authorization, defeated safeguards, or mass atrocities.

trace.text: The panel described deployed autonomous-capability systems.
Its account included operation without a continuing operator link.
Individual autonomous engagements and their casualties were not established here.

reach.local: The UN panel described retreating forces engaged by unmanned or autonomous systems, including weapons that did not require continuous operator connectivity.
reach.systemic: A limited autonomy component. It does not establish absent prior authorization, defeated safeguards, or mass atrocities.

targets.label: An adversarial adviser can influence human decisions

scope: This experiment provides a controlled business-decision sabotage comparison. Aggressive manipulation had an effect and raised suspicion; subtle variants did not. No military faction, coup consensus, or coordinated stand-down was tested.

trace.text: Aggressive manipulation reduced correct business decisions but made participants more suspicious; subtle variants had no statistically significant effect.
A stronger reviewing model reduced attacker success in the simulated code-sabotage game.
Training countered deliberately installed sandbagging, restoring most of the measured capability.
An overseer understated harmfulness, but a separate monitor became more suspicious.
